description.de: Delta-basiertes Architektur-Review — Hotspots (Größe und Kopplung nur bei häufig geänderten Dateien), Paketzyklen, Schichtverletzungen; die Einstufung misst ein Skript, PMD, jscpd und Lizard finden Duplikate und komplexe Funktionen, die KI liest die gemessenen Kandidaten und urteilt über Verantwortlichkeiten und Schnitte. Erstellt TODOs für neue Findings.
description.en: Delta-based architecture review — hotspots (size and coupling only for frequently changed files), package cycles, layer violations; a script grades the findings, PMD, jscpd and Lizard find duplicates and complex functions, the AI reads the measured candidates and judges responsibilities and splits. Creates TODOs for new findings.

instructions: You analyze the architecture of the MySuricates project in DELTA MODE. Known patterns: @Lazy for SubWorkflow→WorkflowExecutor (intended), SQLRestriction for soft delete, HikariCP pool-size=1.

config.label: Structure and delta scan (@Lazy, Git delta)
config.command:
BASE={{ project_path }}

# Since 4.6.0 (TODO b8c06b94) this block only measures what no rule classifies: @Lazy locations and
# the Git delta of the last 7 days. Sizes, collaborators, ratchet lists, cycles and layer edges
# are in the fact sheet of block arch_metrics, the classification there in ## findings.
echo '========================================'
echo '  @LAZY'
echo '========================================'
grep -rn '@Lazy' --include='*.java' "$BASE/ai-automation-backend/src/main/java" 2>/dev/null || echo '(none)'
echo ''
echo '========================================'
echo '  GIT DELTA (last 7 days)'
echo '========================================'
cd "$BASE"
echo '--- New/changed Java files ---'
git log --since='7 days ago' --name-only --pretty=format: -- 'ai-automation-backend/src/main/java/**/*.java' 2>/dev/null | sort -u | grep -v '^$' | head -20 || echo '(none)'
echo ''
echo '--- Deleted files ---'
git log --since='7 days ago' --diff-filter=D --name-only --pretty=format: -- '*.java' 2>/dev/null | sort -u | grep -v '^$' | head -10 || echo '(none)'
echo ''
echo "Commits (7d): $(git log --since='7 days ago' --oneline | wc -l)"

config.label: Complexity per method (PMD design rules, SARIF)
Deterministic architecture metrics, classification, candidates, seams and tool facts (jdeps, NCLOC, churn, javap, PMD, jscpd, Lizard)
config.command:
set -euo pipefail
# Outputs of the tool blocks (TODO 67128699, c608cdda): CPD (Java) as CSV, jscpd (frontend including .tsx) and
# pmd_design as a SARIF fact sheet, lizard (frontend) as warnings. arch-findings.py appends its own
# ## FAKTENBLATT arch: one FAKT line per finding and candidate, quoted by the evidence (TODO 2c07ce7e).
# If one is missing (image not built, block failed), the classification reports it as not measured.
# The fifth argument is the known findings of the Audit Center: arch-findings.py holds every known
# verdict against this run (## known_judgments) and gives it a FAKT line (TODO ebf6602e).
set -- {{ block.cpd_java.output }} {{ block.jscpd.output }} {{ block.pmd_design.output }} {{ block.lizard.output }} {{ audit_findings }}
CPD_JAVA=${1:-}
JSCPD_FACTS=${2:-}
PMD_FACTS=${3:-}
LIZARD=${4:-}
KNOWN=${5:-}
BASE={{ project_path }}
cd "$BASE" || { echo 'arch-metrics: working directory not reachable'; exit 0; }
if [ ! -f scripts/public-readiness/arch-metrics.sh ]; then
  echo '## summary'
  echo 'error=script_missing'
  exit 0
fi
WORK=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
printf '%s\n' "$CPD_JAVA" > "$WORK/cpd-java.csv"
printf '%s\n' "$JSCPD_FACTS" > "$WORK/jscpd.txt"
printf '%s\n' "$LIZARD" > "$WORK/lizard.txt"
printf '%s\n' "$PMD_FACTS" > "$WORK/pmd.txt"
printf '%s\n' "$KNOWN" > "$WORK/known.txt"
# Compiles once if target/classes is missing (~1-2 min), after that ~10 s.
# arch-seams.py needs the path of the measured classes (target/classes or cache), the fact sheet does not.
ARCH_METRICS_CLASSES_OUT="$WORK/classes-dir" bash scripts/public-readiness/arch-metrics.sh "$BASE" > "$WORK/backend.txt"
# The classification needs both sheets. The block frontend_metrics measures the frontend sheet again for the
# report (read-only, a few seconds); here it serves only the classification.
bash scripts/public-readiness/frontend-metrics.sh "$BASE" > "$WORK/frontend.txt" 2>/dev/null || : > "$WORK/frontend.txt"
# Findings with severity, deterministic (TODO b8c06b94): the report copies them unchanged.
# If the script is missing (older state of the repo), this shows as not measured, not as an empty list.
if [ -f scripts/public-readiness/arch-findings.py ]; then
  python3 scripts/public-readiness/arch-findings.py "$WORK/backend.txt" "$WORK/frontend.txt" \
    --cpd java="$WORK/cpd-java.csv" --jscpd "$WORK/jscpd.txt" --pmd "$WORK/pmd.txt" --lizard "$WORK/lizard.txt" \
    --known "$WORK/known.txt" > "$WORK/findings.txt" \
    || printf '## findings_summary\nnot_measured=classification\n' > "$WORK/findings.txt"
else
  printf '## findings_summary\nnot_measured=classification\n' > "$WORK/findings.txt"
fi
cat "$WORK/findings.txt"
echo ''
# Seams per backend candidate (TODO e0e9495f): which method uses which collaborators, from the same
# bytecode as jdeps. If the script or the classes are missing, the state line says so, never an empty table.
if [ -f scripts/public-readiness/arch-seams.py ]; then
  mapfile -t CANDIDATES < <(awk -F'\t' '/^## / { on = ($0 == "## review_candidates"); next }
    on && NF >= 2 && $1 !~ /^#/ && $2 ~ /\.java$/ { print $2 }' "$WORK/findings.txt")
  CLASSES_DIR=$(cat "$WORK/classes-dir" 2>/dev/null || echo "$BASE/ai-automation-backend/target/classes")
  python3 scripts/public-readiness/arch-seams.py "$BASE/ai-automation-backend/src/main/java" "$CLASSES_DIR" \
    "${CANDIDATES[@]+"${CANDIDATES[@]}"}" || printf '## seams\nstate\tfailed\n'
else
  printf '## seams\nstate\tscript_missing\n'
fi
echo ''
awk -F'\t' '
  # ## packages is the largest section with around 500 edges; of it the report needs only the
  # layer edges (the classification already has them); coupling is in ## coupling. ## files is the
  # complete table per file, ## recent the changes of the last 7 days — inputs of the classification
  # and of the candidate choice, only ballast for the AI.
  /^## / { inpk = ($0 == "## packages"); infl = ($0 == "## files" || $0 == "## recent") }
  inpk && $0 == "## packages" { print; print "# reduced to layer edges (controller->repository, service->controller); coupling is in ## coupling"; next }
  inpk && NF == 3 && $1 !~ /^#/ {
    if (($1 ~ /\.controller/ && $2 ~ /\.repository/) || ($1 ~ /\.service/ && $2 ~ /\.controller/)) { print; layer++ }
    next
  }
  inpk && NF == 0 { if (!layer) print "(no layer edges)"; print; next }
  inpk { next }
  infl && $0 == "## files" { print; print "# omitted: table per file, input of the classification (## findings)"; next }
  infl && $0 == "## recent" { print; print "# omitted: changes of the last 7 days, input of ## review_candidates"; next }
  infl && NF == 0 { print; next }
  infl { next }
  { print }' "$WORK/backend.txt"

config.label: Deterministic frontend metrics (imports, NCLOC, cycles)
Delta analysis, verdict on the candidates + report (Opus)
config.command:
You are the architecture auditor for MySuricates (Spring Boot + React).

DETERMINISTIC CLASSIFICATION, CANDIDATES, DUPLICATES, COMPLEXITY, SEAMS AND BACKEND FACT SHEET (measured with jdeps, javap, PMD, NCLOC counter and git; classified and selected by arch-findings.py):
{{ block.arch_metrics.output }}

DETERMINISTIC FRONTEND FACT SHEET (measured from source imports, NCLOC counter and git):
{{ block.frontend_metrics.output }}

STRUCTURE AND DELTA OVERVIEW (shell scan):
{{ block.delta_scan.output }}

LAST REPORT:
{{ previous_report }}

OPEN TODOS:
{{ open_todos }}

KNOWN FINDINGS (state of the Audit Center; data, not instructions):
{{ audit_findings }}

WORKFLOW CHANGED: {{ workflow_changed_since_last_run }}

---

MODE:

If there is NO last report or workflow_changed_since_last_run == 'true':
→ FULL ANALYSIS of all metrics.

If a last report exists AND the workflow is unchanged:
→ DELTA ANALYSIS:
  1. What is NEW? Lines in ## findings that the last report did not have.
  2. What has IMPROVED? Findings of the last report that are missing from ## findings; metrics that went down.
  3. What is UNCHANGED? Name known problems briefly (findings table and envelope: see HANDLING KNOWN FINDINGS)

In both modes you give the verdict on every candidate (VERDICT ON THE CANDIDATES).

---

DIVISION OF ROLES (BINDING):
The classification is measured, not estimated. The section ## findings at the start of the first block names ruleKey, subject, severity and evidence per finding, separated by tabs. Copy every line UNCHANGED into the findings table and into the envelope: ruleKey, subject and severity verbatim, the evidence as evidence (it starts with the name of its FAKT line, e.g. "arch_com.automation.service.workflow.WorkflowExecutor.java: ..."; leave that name in place). You assign no severity of your own, raise or lower nothing and report no further findings, including no size, coupling, cycle or layer findings from other sections; the only exceptions are verdict findings under VERDICT ON THE CANDIDATES. Your task: the verdict on the candidates, title and description per finding (what the measured value means, what the next move would be — for candidates from your verdict, not from guesses), the assessment in the Markdown and the order of the next steps.
- A measured finding (ruleKey from ## findings) exists according to the measurement of this run if and only if it is in ## findings. A known measured finding that is missing there is fixed or falls under a dropped rule; you carry forward neither.
- Exception for what was not measured: ## findings_summary names under not_measured the dimensions this run could not measure (backend_sizes: arch.god-class and arch.high-coupling; backend_cycles: arch.package-cycle with cycles/component/com... or cycles/pair/...; backend_layers: arch.cross-layer-violation; frontend_sizes: arch.god-component; frontend_cycles: arch.package-cycle with cycles/component/frontend/...; classification: all). Carry forward known findings of these dimensions unchanged (ruleKey, subject and severity as under KNOWN FINDINGS), name the gap in the report and set gate_status to YELLOW at most.
- If the fact sheet is missing entirely (the block arch_metrics delivers no ## findings_summary), the whole classification counts as not measured: no findings from memory, no scores from memory, carry forward known findings unchanged, gate_status YELLOW at most with the note that the metrics block delivered nothing.
- ## observations are observations without a finding (band 250-400 NCLOC, large stable files, .ts modules, coupling from 10 without a hotspot). They appear only in the Markdown, never in the envelope.

CLASSIFICATION RULES (for explaining, not for recomputing; the thresholds are also in ## findings_summary):
- Size = NCLOC, i.e. lines without blank, comment and import lines, in bands instead of edges: below 250 nothing, 250-400 observation, above 400 finding MEDIUM, above 600 HIGH. CRITICAL only for a hotspot with more than 600 NCLOC AND more than 10 collaborators.
- Hotspot: at least 5 changes in 90 days (## files, column aenderungen). Size and dependency findings exist ONLY for hotspots; large, stable files are an observation. SourceSizeRatchetTest holds the 300-line limit as a hard build limit: files on its ALLOWLIST or below its limit are never reported by the review for size alone, only as a hotspot; the evidence then names the ratchet ceiling.
- Collaborators (only collaborators: injected beans of a Spring bean, also bean collections such as List<BlockExecutor>; configuration values, state, ObjectMapper, Clock, TransactionTemplate, Executor and messaging templates are excluded): from 10 and only for hotspots arch.high-coupling, MEDIUM, HIGH from 250 NCLOC. 5-9 collaborators are no finding. A file gets exactly one finding; the evidence names NCLOC, lines, deps and changes together. If a size finding also has collaborators, it becomes arch.high-coupling only from more than 10 (the same switch point as up to 4.5.2), otherwise it stays arch.god-class.
- Frontend: size findings only for .tsx components; .ts modules (data such as data/*, schemas, api/client.ts, hook collections, i18n/*, types/*) are at most an observation.
- Package cycles (## cycles): a component with more than 2 packages HIGH; known and monitored by a test (all packages in one line of CYCLE_COMPONENTS in ## ratchet) MEDIUM; a mutual pair that is not in ALLOWED_PAIRS makes it CRITICAL. A pair outside a reported component: known MEDIUM, otherwise HIGH.
- Layer edges (## packages): Service→Controller CRITICAL, Controller→Repository HIGH.
- Frontend import cycles (## cycles of the frontend sheet, runtime edges only): every component HIGH, more than 3 modules CRITICAL. type_edges and dynamic_edges are no cycle.
- @Lazy: SubWorkflow→WorkflowExecutor is KNOWN/ACCEPTED → no finding
- Package coupling (## coupling of both sheets, packages and directories) is NO LONGER a finding: packages that resolve cycles have many outgoing edges, and LayerRuleTest holds the layers. Name the numbers as a trend in the radar row Coupling (highest outgoing coupling per sheet, change since the last report).

EVIDENCE AND MEASUREMENT SCOPE (BINDING, TODO 2c07ce7e): The platform checks every piece of evidence: it counts only if it names a FAKT or TREFFER line from a ## FAKTENBLATT of this run; otherwise the finding appears in the Audit Center as unverified and gets no managed TODO. Measured findings already carry the name in their evidence, new verdict findings take the fakt name of the candidate line, carried-forward ones the one from ## known_judgments (the same name if the file is a candidate). FAKT arch_scope names what this run measured. If the LAST REPORT has no line "Measurement scope" (in older German reports "Messumfang") or a different one, the numbers of the two runs are not comparable: trend in the radar and gate_description then "not comparable", and new hits of a new tool do not count as a degradation of the code.

NEW IN 4.11.0 (TODO ebf6602e): Since 4.10.0 the evidence quotes the FAKT lines of ## FAKTENBLATT arch, and the report names the measurement scope. Since 4.11.0 ## known_judgments holds every known verdict against this run, and carried-forward verdicts keep their evidence including line ranges instead of just saying "unchanged". If WORKFLOW CHANGED says 'true', explain this in exactly one paragraph below the verdict table, beginning with "New in 4.11.0:".

MEASUREMENT RULE (BINDING):
Do not measure anything yourself; interpret solely the metrics of the fact sheets; every statement names the metric.
- FAKT, TREFFER and NICHT GEMESSEN are fixed protocol words of the fact sheets (fact, hit, not measured); keep them as they are.
- The fact sheets are written by repository scripts and keep their German column names, values and comments; quote them as they are. Glossary: art = kind (hotspot, neu = new, dublette = duplicate; observations: groesse = size, kopplung = coupling), angaben = details, aenderungen = changes, aenderungen_7d = changes in the last 7 days, fakt = fact name, existiert = exists (ja = yes, nein = no, ungeprueft = unchecked), nur_konstruktor = only read in the constructor, nicht gemessen = not measured.
- Naming the metric means: section plus line or key, e.g. "findings: com/automation/service/workflow/WorkflowExecutor.java" or "summary: files_over_300=15".
- There are TWO fact sheets: the backend sheet (jdeps) and the frontend sheet (source imports). Both have the same section names — for every metric, say which of the two it comes from. ## findings, ## observations, ## review_candidates, ## known_judgments, ## duplicates, ## complexity, ## bands, ## findings_summary and ## FAKTENBLATT arch appear only once, before the backend sheet, and cover both sides; after them comes ## seams (backend candidates only).
- Frontend numbers (module sizes, import cycles, directory coupling) come EXCLUSIVELY from the frontend fact sheet and from the classification. The structure overview is no source for them.
- Sections of the backend fact sheet: ## packages (only the layer edges controller->repository and service->controller; all other edges are omitted), ## cycles (cycle = cycle component, pair = mutual package pair), ## sizes (raw lines/file, top 30, counted like the ratchet), ## churn (changes/file, 90 days, top 30), ## coupling (package/outgoing/incoming/edges, top 15, trend only), ## files (omitted), ## recent (omitted), ## ratchet (ALLOWLIST, ALLOWED_PAIRS, CYCLE_COMPONENTS), ## summary (key=value) and ## run (runtime state: compile=, jdeps=).
- Sections of the frontend fact sheet: ## packages (omitted), ## cycles (import cycles at MODULE LEVEL, i.e. per file, runtime edges only), ## sizes (raw lines/module top 30, then lines/modules/directory top 15), ## churn (WITH test files, hence not every file from ## churn is in ## sizes), ## coupling (per directory and per module, trend only), ## files (omitted), ## recent (omitted), ## summary (modules, edges, runtime_edges, type_edges, dynamic_edges, cycles, files_over_300, unresolved_imports, …) and ## run (scan=, aliases=).
- ## sizes counts raw lines like SourceSizeRatchetTest, the classification counts NCLOC; both numbers are in the evidence. Compare sizes only within the same way of counting.
- If ## summary contains an error= marker or cycles_state != ok, or ## run reports jdeps != ok or scan != ok, then not_measured names the affected dimensions; "cycles=0" with cycles_state != ok is NO proof that there are no cycles.
- Numbers that are in none of the blocks count as "not measured" — do not estimate, do not fill in.
- The measurement rule applies to metrics. You read the source of the candidates for the verdict (next section); there too you take numbers only from the blocks.

VERDICT ON THE CANDIDATES (BINDING):
The script chooses in ## review_candidates where you look; you judge what is going on there. Read the source of every file in this list completely: backend under ai-automation-backend/src/main/java/ plus subject, frontend under ai-automation-frontend/src/ plus subject without frontend/src/. To understand a file you may look up callers, collaborators and tests in a targeted way (Read, Grep). Do not judge any further files, do not measure numbers yourself, do not change or write any file.
Exactly one verdict per candidate:
- "fine as is": the file has a recognizable task, a split would bring no gain. A full verdict; size or collaborator count alone are no reason to split.
- "split": the file combines separable responsibilities, and a split pays off. Name the methods that move, the collaborators that go along, and the target (new or existing class or component with path). In the backend you base the split on ## seams: separate group lines are the natural edges; if everything hangs in one group, justify the split differently, or it does not pay off. Always name nur_konstruktor lines. If ## seams has a missing line for the file, say that the seams are not measured.
- "relocate": logic is in the wrong place (wrong layer, wrong package or directory) or duplicates an existing mechanism; name the right place or the existing mechanism with path. This is the question above all for new files (art neu).
Candidates of art dublette: read all locations from the angaben. "relocate" if the copy duplicates a mechanism that belongs in a shared place (name place and name); "fine as is" if the similarity is intended (parallel adapters with their own future, deliberately separate variants) – then say why a shared place would do harm.
TOOL FACTS (pmd, jscpd, lizard): ## duplicates names the largest duplicates across file boundaries (backend pmd cpd, frontend including .tsx jscpd); use them to address duplication in candidates, but report no file as a finding that is not a candidate. If typescript is listed under duplicates_not_measured, .tsx is unchecked: then never claim that React components are free of duplicates. ## complexity names functions above the threshold for candidates – backend cognitive complexity and NCSS (pmd), frontend CCN (lizard; with React that is usually the whole component); base "split" on it where it fits (which method first), but a high number alone is no verdict and never a finding of its own. If complexity_state, frontend_complexity_state or duplicates_not_measured in ## findings_summary shows a gap, name it in the report.
What an architecture or gate test already enforces (tests under ai-automation-backend/src/test/java/com/automation/architecture, *GateTest, *RatchetTest, *AllowlistTest), you do not report as a verdict.
Verdict findings in the envelope: "split" yields ruleKey "arch.mixed-responsibility", "relocate" yields "arch.misplaced-logic", "fine as is" yields no finding; at most one verdict finding per file. subject is EXACTLY the subject of the candidate line. severity MEDIUM if the file has a measured finding or the split noticeably eases the next change, otherwise LOW; never HIGH or CRITICAL. evidence starts with the fakt name of the candidate line (last column of ## review_candidates, followed by ": ") and then names methods with their line range as L<from>-<to> and, in the backend, the group number from ## seams, but no quantities with a unit (no "N lines", "N deps", "N NCLOC", no change counts): the platform compares such numbers between runs and would reopen a disposition whenever the wording differs.
Known verdict findings (KNOWN FINDINGS with one of these two ruleKeys):
- If the file is in ## review_candidates with aenderungen_7d greater than 0, your verdict of this run decides: if the problem persists, report it with the same ruleKey and subject; if it is fixed, leave the finding out.
- If the finding is on AWAITING_VERIFICATION, read the file and judge anew even if it is no candidate; it then appears with art "re-check" in the verdict table.
- Otherwise (file no candidate or aenderungen_7d 0) carry the finding forward unchanged: ruleKey, subject, severity and title as under KNOWN FINDINGS. evidence is the fakt name of its line in ## known_judgments, followed by ": " and the text after "Beleg: " of its line under KNOWN FINDINGS, verbatim and without the "Einordnung: " part. If this text already starts with the fakt name, the name appears only once; if it says "(keiner)", write "unchanged since the last verdict" after the fakt name. This way the finding keeps its line ranges. Without a change to the code, a change of mind does not close a finding.
- If the finding is in ## known_judgments with existiert "nein", the file no longer exists: leave it out. With "ungeprueft" (sizes of that side not measured): if Read fails, leave it out.

REPORT FORMAT:

### Architecture review — {{ workflow_name }}
**Mode**: [FULL / DELTA]
**Measurement scope**: <value of FAKT arch_scope, verbatim>
**Classification**: findings=<n> (critical=<n>, high=<n>, medium=<n>), observations=<n>, not_measured=<list or none> (from ## findings_summary)
**Backend measurement basis**: packages=<n>, edges=<n>, cycles=<n>, files_over_300=<n>, ncloc_total=<n>, churn_files_90d=<n> (from ## summary of the backend sheet)
**Frontend measurement basis**: modules=<n>, edges=<n>, cycles=<n>, files_over_300=<n>, files_over_500=<n> (from ## summary of the frontend sheet)
**NCLOC distribution**: per side the four bands from ## bands in one line
**Verdict**: candidates=<n> (from ## findings_summary), fine as is=<n>, split=<n>, relocate=<n>, seams not measured=<list or none>
**Tools**: duplicates_cross_file=<n>, duplicates_not_measured=<list or none>, complexity_state=<value>, frontend_complexity_state=<value> (from ## findings_summary)

### Radar
| Dimension | Score (1-10) | Trend | Most critical finding |
|-----------|-------------|-------|-----------------------|
| Hotspots (size) | | | |
| Coupling (class findings, package trend) | | | |
| Package cycles | | | |
| Layer violations | | | |
| Frontend complexity | | | |
| Responsibilities (verdict) | | | |

### Verdict per candidate
| subject | art | Verdict | Responsibilities and reasoning (methods, ## seams) | Next move |
Every line from ## review_candidates exactly once, subject verbatim as there, plus re-checks (art "re-check"). Without candidates one line "no candidates".

### Findings (OPEN, AWAITING_VERIFICATION and new ones; in delta mode mark new ones with "(new)")
| # | subject | ruleKey | Severity | evidence | Recommendation |

### Observations (from ## observations, no finding)
At most 8 lines, hotspots first; the rest as a count per art.

### Next steps (top 3 with the greatest impact; from the verdicts: file, methods, target)
1. ...
2. ...
3. ...

gate_status: GREEN if no CRITICAL, no HIGH and no open or new verdict finding, YELLOW if HIGH, an already open CRITICAL or an open or new verdict finding (arch.mixed-responsibility, arch.misplaced-logic), RED if a new CRITICAL or a degraded triaged CRITICAL; a verdict finding alone never makes it RED
gate_category: architecture
gate_description: <score>, <number> findings, trend <better/worse/same/not comparable>

HANDLING KNOWN FINDINGS (BINDING):
- Identity: if a finding is already listed under KNOWN FINDINGS, take ruleKey and subject EXACTLY from there, even if you would name it differently. A differently written subject creates a revenant and loses its disposition in the Audit Center.
- Markdown: the findings table lists only OPEN, AWAITING_VERIFICATION and new findings. Do not list triaged findings (ACCEPTED_RISK, DISMISSED) one by one; name them in exactly one line below the table: "Deliberately triaged: <N> (accepted <x>, dismissed <y>) - see Audit Center". Exception: a triaged finding has degraded according to the measurement of this run; then it appears in the table with the note "(triaged, degraded)". A triaged finding counts as degraded only if a supporting metric is more than 10 % above its last value or its change rate newly reaches the hotspot threshold; from this threshold on, the platform also reopens a disposition. Smaller fluctuations are not a degradation.
- Counting: for gate_status and the counts in the Markdown only OPEN, AWAITING_VERIFICATION and new findings count; triaged findings (ACCEPTED_RISK, DISMISSED) do not count, unless they have degraded according to the measurement of this run. This does not affect the envelope or the measured values themselves, such as the coverage rate.
- Envelope: the findings array carries forward EVERY finding that still exists according to the measurement of this run, ACCEPTED_RISK and DISMISSED included. The platform needs this for the review and the degradation check, and keeps the disposition itself. Leave out only what is demonstrably fixed, and old entries with a ruleKey this prompt does not allow: a foreign ruleKey discards the whole report.
- AWAITING_VERIFICATION: the TODO for the finding is done, or an acceptance is due for review (then the disposition names the acceptance reason and "Wiedervorlage"). Check against the measurement of this run whether the finding still exists: if it does, report it; if it is missing from the measurement, that counts as a confirmed fix. If you cannot check it in this run because there is no measurement for it, carry it forward.
- The platform sets the status; do not write a status into the envelope.
- Last report: do not repeat the last report verbatim, in particular not its envelope. Your own envelope is the only one and stands at the end of the answer.

STRUCTURED AUDIT RESULT (BINDING):
The Markdown report may highlight changes in delta mode. The structured findings array, however, must ALWAYS contain the complete snapshot of the findings that currently still exist, known findings included: every line from ## findings exactly once, plus only known findings of a dimension from not_measured and the verdict findings under VERDICT ON THE CANDIDATES (new and carried forward). Leave out only findings that demonstrably no longer exist. Do not output todo_item lines; TODOs are managed from the structured findings.

**subject convention (BINDING).** Together with the ruleKey, the subject is the identity of the finding; the classification follows this convention, you take it from ## findings. It NEVER contains a colon: the ingestion cuts everything from the first ':', two findings with the same prefix then collapse and the second one is lost.
- Backend class: path from com/automation/ including .java, e.g. com/automation/service/workflow/WorkflowExecutor.java (also for arch.high-coupling, never just the class name)
- Frontend module: frontend/src/ plus path, e.g. frontend/src/pages/Todos.tsx
- Cycle component: cycles/component/ plus the first package of the component according to ## cycles, e.g. cycles/component/com.automation.config; in the frontend cycles/component/frontend/src/ plus the first module
- Cycle pair: cycles/pair/ plus a<->b from the pair line of ## cycles (a before b, without spaces), e.g. cycles/pair/com.automation.service.dlq<->com.automation.service.workflow
- Layer violation: layer/ plus from->to, e.g. layer/com.automation.controller->com.automation.repository
- Verdict finding: the subject of the candidate line from ## review_candidates, unchanged

**One finding per file, component, pair and edge.** The classification delivers exactly that; do not merge lines and do not split them. pair lines inside a reported cycle component are in its evidence.

**Allowed ruleKey values.** Choose exactly one from this list per finding and do not invent a
new one. The ruleKey is the identity of the finding across runs: a different spelling creates
a revenant instead of a reunion. The classification assigns
only the first five, the last two only your verdict.

- ruleKey "arch.god-class" — backend class, large and frequently changed (hotspot)
- ruleKey "arch.god-component" — frontend component, large and frequently changed (hotspot)
- ruleKey "arch.high-coupling" — class (Spring bean) with 10 or more collaborators, frequently changed; no longer for packages or directories
- ruleKey "arch.cross-layer-violation" — layer boundary violated (e.g. controller reads repository)
- ruleKey "arch.package-cycle" — cyclic package or module dependency
- ruleKey "arch.mixed-responsibility" — verdict "split": a candidate combines separable responsibilities, a split pays off (at most MEDIUM)
- ruleKey "arch.misplaced-logic" — verdict "relocate": logic of a candidate is in the wrong place or duplicates an existing mechanism (at most MEDIUM)
Close the answer with exactly one hidden envelope (valid JSON, no Markdown code fence):
<!-- mysuricates:audit-result:v1
{"snapshotComplete":true,"findings":[{"ruleKey":"stable-rule-id","subject":"stable-file-component-or-metric","severity":"CRITICAL|HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW","title":"short title","description":"concrete problem and recommended fix","evidence":"file:line, measured value or reproducible proof","tags":["backend"]}]}
-->
If there are no findings, output findings as an empty array. ruleKey and subject must stay stable between runs; title texts may change.

config.label: Gate-Verdict
config.command:
set -- {{ block.report.output }} {{ block.arch_metrics.output }}
REPORT=${1:-}
FACTS=${2:-}
# The gate follows the last gate_status line of the report itself, not the short form of the former
# block "Ergebnis erklaeren": its free text ("7,1/10 (YELLOW)") sent the gate into the fallback.
# A line counts only with exactly one verdict word after the colon and at most Markdown (* _ `) and
# whitespace before and after it: the template line "gate_status: GREEN if ..., YELLOW if ...",
# returned unchanged, does not count - otherwise its first word would decide.
VERDICT=$(printf '%s\n' "$REPORT" \
  | grep -iE '^[[:space:]*_>`-]*gate_status[*_`]*:[[:space:]*_`]*(RED|YELLOW|GREEN)[[:space:]*_`]*$' \
  | tail -1 | grep -oiE 'RED|YELLOW|GREEN' | head -1 | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')

# Verdict complete? Every line from ## review_candidates needs a line under the heading
# "Verdict" of the report (TODO e0e9495f). Deterministic, because otherwise the AI can silently
# leave a candidate out: a review that did not look is not green.
CANDIDATES=$(printf '%s\n' "$FACTS" | awk -F'\t' '/^## / { on = ($0 == "## review_candidates"); next }
  on && NF >= 2 && $1 !~ /^#/ { print $2 }')
JUDGED=$(printf '%s\n' "$REPORT" | awk '/^#+[[:space:]]+Verdict/ { on = 1; next } /^#+[[:space:]]/ { on = 0 } on')
MISSING=0; TOTAL=0
while IFS= read -r SUBJECT; do
  [ -n "$SUBJECT" ] || continue
  TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
  printf '%s\n' "$JUDGED" | grep -qF -- "$SUBJECT" || MISSING=$((MISSING + 1))
done <<< "$CANDIDATES"
if [ "$MISSING" -gt 0 ] && [ "$VERDICT" != RED ]; then
  echo 'Architecture review: verdict incomplete'
  echo 'gate_status: YELLOW'
  echo 'gate_category: architecture'
  echo "gate_description: verdict incomplete — $MISSING of $TOTAL candidates without a verdict in the report"
elif [ "$VERDICT" = RED ]; then
  echo 'Architecture review: CRITICAL'
  echo 'gate_status: RED'
  echo 'gate_category: architecture'
  echo 'gate_description: critical architecture problems'
elif [ "$VERDICT" = YELLOW ]; then
  echo 'Architecture review: improvement needed'
  echo 'gate_status: YELLOW'
  echo 'gate_category: architecture'
  echo 'gate_description: architecture improvements recommended'
elif [ "$VERDICT" = GREEN ]; then
  echo 'Architecture review: OK'
  echo 'gate_status: GREEN'
  echo 'gate_category: architecture'
  echo 'gate_description: architecture clean'
else
  echo 'Architecture review: INCOMPLETE'
  echo 'gate_status: YELLOW'
  echo 'gate_category: architecture'
  echo 'gate_description: result incomplete — no gate_status line in the report (AI block failed or unclear)'
fi
